title: Wire UI runtime architecture: server truth, renderer access points
summary: Wire UI is a renderer-neutral, queue-connected presentation protocol. Authoritative application truth lives in ooRexx/server objects; Web, Swing, GTK/Direct Linux and Android are peer access points that consume the same semantic state and emit the same semantic actions.
invariants: Business state, journey state, security decisions, pricing and transaction authority remain server-side.
Web, Swing, GTK/Direct Linux and Android are access points, never independent application models.
Stable semantic element identity is not a DOM node, JComponent, GtkWidget, Android View/Compose node or HWND.
Builder authoring truth is semantic and renderer-neutral; toolkit construction never enters ordinary application Rexx.
Queue Fabric remains the live transport substrate where remote transport is used; HTTP/static delivery does not become a second business API.
Semantic activation enters Wire action/event machinery and never synthesizes toolkit-native input.
procedure: Bind the running application to an exact compiled site release.
Select an authorised renderer profile from capability facts.
Deliver exact definitions/material/resource references required by active subscriptions.
Render the authoritative snapshot and revisioned patches.
Return only semantic actions carrying exact rendered-revision context.

provenance.claim: Cross-renderer doctrine, stable identity, semantic activation, Android convergence and WireUIProxy boundary.
